methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native directly address the distribution challenge, representing grassroots peer-to-peer capability building that could enable deep understanding outside traditional tech hubs if sustained and scaled.

signals.title: Virginia Tech, Children’s National Spark Pediatric AI Innovation Hub to Speed Research, Care | Newswise - Newswise
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's pediatric AI hub partnership consolidates research-grade AI capability in an established institution, deepening technical excellence in ways that may remain concentrated unless deliberate knowledge transfer mechanisms reach community healthcare providers statewide.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly naming data center concentration in NoVA as driver of urban-rural divide signals recognition that current infrastructure deployment patterns reinforce geographic inequality without distributing AI capability benefits.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M AI infrastructure investment adding 200 jobs in Henrico strengthens Richmond's position as a secondary AI hub, but hardware deployment alone doesn't guarantee distributed capability unless workforce development reaches beyond metro boundaries.

signals.title: Virginia journalist: Fired by AI - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: AI-driven journalism layoffs demonstrate platform automation creating broad but shallow workforce displacement rather than capability enhancement—a critical signal that distribution without depth may undermine rather than strengthen Virginia's human capital.
